newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases as investors offload.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases as investors offload.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index fell 12.64 points to 3516.57 on Wednesday as investors offloaded key shares into the market, brokers said.
Turnover was posted at 34.206 million shillings on 541,061 shares from 24.314 million shares on 521,512 shares on Tuesday, boosted by two deals on the one-hour special board.
Uchumi Supermarket and Kenya Power & Lighting traded at reserve prices of 44.25 from 40 and 125 from 133 respectively on the special board.
Brokers said Kenya Power & Lighting Co, which made great gains in January after its year-end announcement, was now consolidating itself and selling at a realistic price.
They added that the price eased on an excess supply caused by investors who were offloading their shares.
Uchumi Supermarket, which suffered a loss of 400 million shillings ($7.4 million) from a fire that destroyed all its warehouses on Sunday night, remained unchanged at 40.
Suresh Shah, the supermarket's managing director, said that the fire would make a reasonable initial dent on the company's sales but did not see a conclusive loss.
"Overall, I do not see a loss as we are quite covered by insurance and the employees are putting extra effort to compensate for any losses," Shah told Reuters.

He expressed confidence that investors would not panic even if their final investment decision was their prerogative -- "I am doing my best to keep my part, which is my responsibility to shareholders, I am confident the price will remain stable."

Foreign investors maintained their support for selected shares, buying Firestone East Africa at between 30-30.75 from 30; Kenya Commercial Bank at 92.50 and 93 from 92; and Kenya Breweries 1,000 shares at 53 unchanged.
Other shares were stable; Barclays Bank was unchanged at 120 while Standard Chartered Bank edged to 56.50 from 56. Kenya Airways fell to 8.80 and 8.85.
"Our market will remain on hold until after the results -- mostly the financials are released. Maybe after that we will be able to tell the market's direction," a senior broker said.
